A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MM-Traj/T3-Agent research work. Their complete main text, Tables 1–9, Figures 1–24, and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GTA/GAIA evaluations, human studies, verifier and image-modality ablations, and data-size experiments in the main text and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, human studies, ablations, and data-size experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds T to the conditioning in both inference and training probabilities in Equations (1)–(2), without explaining a procedural change. Section 3.1 defines T as generated thoughts, while the workflow, architecture, tools, and prompts remain unchanged. Whether this represents an intended input change or a formula error is unresolved.

E1.justification: The MM-Traj source collections, auxiliary training datasets, and GTA/GAIA evaluation coverage remain unchanged. Changing 'more than 9 files' to 'more than 9 kinds of files' clarifies existing coverage rather than adding file types or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same Lego Agent and HF Agent comparisons and controller variants. Table 3 retains the same Sibyl Agent, Warm-up Act, and HF Agent comparisons. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The stated training and evaluation settings remain unchanged, including five training epochs, LoRA settings, GTA metrics, the GAIA validation evaluation, and human-study sample sizes and procedures. Appendix experimental settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the verifier ablation in Table 5, human studies in Appendix A, image-removal and data-size analyses in Tables 8–9, and the same case studies. Appendix material printed in red in v1 is retained in black in v2, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates, human-rating averages, and preference percentages. Neither adds or revises repeated-run information, seeds, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative outcomes remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, tuned MiniCPM-V retains GTA AnsAcc 52.56 and GAIA AnsAcc 15.15, while Table 7 retains 66% preference for the tuned agent.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2) change P(t_i,c_i | F_opt,Q,h_i) to P(t_i,c_i | F_opt,T,Q,h_i). This alters the stated mathematical conditioning, rather than merely its typography, although the added dependency is unexplained. No theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about multimodal data synthesis, the 20K-task MM-Traj dataset, and improved tool use through T3-Agent tuning.

C2.justification: Interpretations of verifier effectiveness, image dependence, data scaling, and benchmark performance remain unchanged. The limitation that multimodal information is used in queries but not intermediate agent trajectories is also retained.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, resource figures in Table 9, tool implementations in Appendix C, prompts in Appendix D, and project/access links are unchanged. No additional operational explanation accompanies the equation edits.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and comparisons with earlier research remain unchanged. The new ICLR publication header does not revise the scientific positioning.

P1.justification: v2 replaces the preprint header with the ICLR 2025 publication header and makes localized wording and capitalization corrections, including 'kinds of files' in Section 3.6.1. Section order and narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 removes red highlighting from appendix text and Tables 6–9, capitalizes the MM-Traj label in Figure 2, and slightly resizes/repositions an audio icon in Figure 5. Figure/table organization and substantive visual content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides small wording and visual-consistency improvements, but adds unexplained T-conditioning to the inference and training equations even though Section 3.1 defines T as generated thoughts. Experimental evidence and substantive discussion remain unchanged. Whether the equation edit clarifies the intended model or introduces a formal error is unresolved, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
